PRODUCT_VARIANT_NAME: Enrofloxacin-d5
PRODUCT_NAME: Enrofloxacin-d5
DESCRIPTION: Enrofloxacin-d5 is intended for use as an internal standard for the quantification of enrofloxacin by GC- or LC-MS. Enrofloxacin is a fluoroquinolone antibiotic. It is active against panels of Campylobacter, E. coli, and Salmonella isolates (mean MIC50s = 0.06, 0.5, and 0.03 ug/ml, respectively). It is also active against equine isolates of L. intracellularis (MICs = 0.125-0.5 ug/ml). Enrofloxacin inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase. In vivo, enrofloxacin (10 mg/kg) increases survival in a mouse model of enteropathogenic E. coli-induced sepsis. Formulations containing enrofloxacin have been used in the treatment of veterinary bacterial infections.

Besides elastase activity, MMP-12 shows broad substrate specificity on ECM proteins such as fibronectin, laminin, vitronectin, type IV collagen and heparan sulfate, while having no proteolytic activity on type I collagen. Accordingly, MMP-12 not only digests elastin but also degrades the basement membrane, which allows macrophages to penetrate into injured tissue during inflammation. Inhibitors may be useful for cancer, rheumatoid arthritis, autoimmune diseases, periodontitis, tissue ulcerlation, atherosclerosis, aneurysm and heart failure.

Inhibitors may be useful for cancer, rheumatoid arthritis, autoimmune diseases, periodontitis, tissue ulcerlation, atherosclerosis, aneurysm and heart failure.

On the basis of their preferred substrates, they can be divided into four main classes: collagenases, gelatinases, stromelysins and membrane-type MMPs. These enzymes demonstrate very low activity in normal tissue but are upregulated and/or activated during inflammation and physiological remodeling processes in response to specific stimuli, including cytokines, growth factors and extracellular matrix interactions. MMP-12 (macrophage elastase) was first identified as an elastolytic metalloproteinase secreted by inflammatory macrophages. Besides elastase activity, MMP-12 shows broad substrate specificity on ECM proteins such as fibronectin, laminin, vitronectin, type IV collagen and heparan sulfate, while having no proteolytic activity on type I collagen. Accordingly, MMP-12 not only digests elastin but also degrades the basement membrane, which allows macrophages to penetrate into injured tissue during inflammation. Inhibitors may be useful for cancer, rheumatoid arthritis, autoimmune diseases, periodontitis, tissue ulcerlation, atherosclerosis, aneurysm and heart failure.
